// reference/src/semantics/core.k — MPY-CORE

module MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-SYNTAX
  imports INT
  imports BOOL
  imports STRING
  imports MAP
  imports LIST
  imports K-EQUAL

  // ==== values, the algebraic lists, and the scope heap =====================
  syntax IntSeq ::= ".IntSeq" | iCons(Int, IntSeq)
  syntax ValSeq ::= ".ValSeq" | vCons(Val, ValSeq)
  syntax Str    ::= str(IntSeq)

  // the iterable values, grouped under one sort (typing only — dispatch is <k>-cell)
  syntax Iterable ::= list(ValSeq)
                    | tuple(ValSeq)
                    | Str
                    | rangeObj(Int, Int, Int)
                    | zipObj(ValSeq, ValSeq)
                    | zipObjS(IntSeq, IntSeq)

  syntax Val      ::= Int
                    | Bool
                    | "noneV"
                    | Iterable
                    | ref(Int)          // a heap object: <heap> holds its list(VS)
                    | cellRef(Int)      // a closure cell: <heap> holds cellV(V)
                    | closureVal(ParamNames, Stmts, Int)
                    | typeV(String)     // a type object (int/str), resolved from the builtins frame
                    | builtinV(String)  // a builtin function, resolved like any name (LEGB fallthrough)
                    | boundMethodV(Val, String)   // a cooled Attribute: obj.method

  syntax Parent   ::= "root" | parent(Int)
  syntax Scope    ::= scope(Map, Parent)
  syntax KResult  ::= Val
  syntax Expr     ::= Val   // cooling puts results back into expression holes
  syntax Vals     ::= List{Val, ","}
  syntax Exc      ::= "NoExc" | "AssertionError"
  syntax RetState ::= "noRet" | retV(Val)

  // ==== configuration =======================================================
  // The builtins namespace is a real scope at reserved location -1 (the bottom of every
  // chain; scopeLoc only allocates >=1, so -1 never collides). The module scope (loc 0)
  // has it as parent, so an unbound name resolves there last — exactly LEGB. `int`/`str`
  // resolve to their type objects; any local/global binding shadows them via normal lookup.
  configuration
    <k>       #loadAll($PGM:Module) </k>
    <env>     0 </env>
    <scopes>   0     |-> scope(.Map, parent(-1))
              -1    |-> builtinsScope </scopes>
    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>
    <heap>    .Map </heap>
    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    <stack>   .List </stack>
    <ret>     noRet </ret>
    <exc>     NoExc </exc>
    <exit-code exit=""> 0 </exit-code>

  // ==== heap allocation (constructed lists become objects) ==================
  // Cons-form emission with a freshness guard (the heap-list-probe discipline:
  // an update-form H[N <- _] never re-normalizes symbolically). heapLoc is
  // monotonic — it does NOT wind back at #pop: returned lists escape by ref.
  // A bare list(VS) Val stays legal (read-only inputs in claims flow unboxed);
  // only CONSTRUCTORS in program syntax allocate.
  syntax Bool ::= isRefV(Val) [function, total]
  rule isRefV(ref(_:Int)) => true
  rule isRefV(_:Val)      => false [owise]

  // closure cells (Python-faithful capture): the heap holds cellV(V); a
  // cellRef surfacing as the k-redex reads through (lookup is the only use —
  // cellRefs never escape to user-visible values)
  syntax HeapVal ::= cellV(Val)
  syntax Bool ::= isCellRef(Val) [function, total]
  rule isCellRef(cellRef(_:Int)) => true
  rule isCellRef(_:Val)          => false [owise]
  // k-top deref for cell-bound reads surfacing INSIDE the annotated frame
  // (AugAssign's in-place read and friends). The "$cells" guard keeps this
  // DECIDABLY inapplicable in plain frames — an unguarded rule lets the
  // prover narrow abstract k-top values into cellRef junk (probed on
  // 26-remove-duplicates). Cross-frame reads (a comprehension closure
  // reading the enclosing function's cellvar) deref inside #look instead.
  rule <k> cellRef(H:Int) => V ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
       [priority(40)]

  // write through a cell (Assign / #bindP / #bindTgt dispatch here on
  // cell-bound names)
  // a keyword argument cools to a TAGGED value (consumed by kw-aware builtins)
  syntax Val ::= kwV(String, Val)
  syntax KItem ::= #kwTag(String)
  rule <k> KwArg(N:String, E:Expr) => E ~> #kwTag(N) ... </k>
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #kwTag(N:String) => kwV(N, V) ... </k>
       requires notBool isKwV(V)
  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]

  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)

  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>

  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)
  rule <k> #alloc(V:Val) => ref(N) ... </k>
       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
       requires notBool N in_keys(H)

  // ==== module load + statement sequencing ==================================
  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>

  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M)
  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
       [priority(40)]
  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))

  // the ONE predefined builtins scope (the -1 frame; claims write `-1 |-> builtinsScope`)
  syntax Scope ::= "builtinsScope" [function, total]
  rule builtinsScope
    => scope(.Map [ "len"    <- builtinV("len")    ]
                  [ "set"    <- builtinV("set")    ]
                  [ "sum"    <- builtinV("sum")    ]
                  [ "abs"    <- builtinV("abs")    ]
                  [ "min"    <- builtinV("min")    ]
                  [ "max"    <- builtinV("max")    ]
                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)

  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>

  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>

  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)

  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]

  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)

  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))

  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)
  syntax Int ::= vsLen(ValSeq) [function, total]
  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)

  syntax Int ::= isLen(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule isLen(.IntSeq)                => 0
  rule isLen(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq)) => 1 +Int isLen(S)

  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]
  rule setVSAt(.ValSeq, _:Int, _:Val)               => .ValSeq
  rule setVSAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), 0, V:Val)    => vCons(V, S)
  rule setVSAt(vCons(W:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int, V:Val) => vCons(W, setVSAt(S, I -Int 1, V))
       requires I >Int 0
  rule setVSAt(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, _:Val)             => VS
       requires I <Int 0
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/functions.k — MPY-FUNCTIONS

module MPY-FUNCTIONS
  imports MPY-CORE

  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
                 | "#pop"
                 | "#endcall"

  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>

  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>

  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)

  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires FV in_keys(M)
  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>

  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires FV in_keys(M)
  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>

  // ==== bind params ========================================================
  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/controls.k — MPY-CONTROLS

module MPY-CONTROLS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-TUPLE
  imports MPY-ITER

  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M)
  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
       [priority(40)]

  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
       <env> L:Int </env>
       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")

  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>

  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>

  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"

  rule <k> For(…6958 tokens truncated…alse         requires A  >Int B
  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B

  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
endmodule
// reference/src/semantics/builtins.k — MPY-BUILTINS

module MPY-BUILTINS
  imports MPY-CORE
  imports MPY-STR
  imports MPY-SET
  imports MPY-ITER
  imports MPY-RANGE
  imports MPY-INT
  imports MPY-METHODS

  // the builtins REGISTRY is core.k's builtinsScope (the -1 frame); names resolve by lookup

  // Call routing + argument evaluation live in call.k, which also routes the fold
  // builtins (sum/all/any/max/min) to the #_Acc folds below and everything else to
  // applyBuiltin. This module owns applyBuiltin + the fold implementations.
  syntax Val ::= applyBuiltin(String, Vals) [function]

  // ==== len(obj) — O(1) per kind ============================================
  syntax Int ::= seqLen(Val) [function]
  rule applyBuiltin("len", OBJ:Val, .Vals) => seqLen(OBJ)
  rule seqLen(list(VS:ValSeq))                  => vsLen(VS)
  rule seqLen(tuple(VS:ValSeq))                 => vsLen(VS)
  rule seqLen(str(IS:IntSeq))                   => isLen(IS)
  rule seqLen(setV(DS:IntSeq))                  => isLen(DS)
  rule seqLen(rangeObj(LO:Int, HI:Int, ST:Int)) => rangeLen(LO, HI, ST)

  // ==== list(seq) — materialize a list/tuple into a list (e.g. list(d.keys())) ==
  // Minimal: the "copy a sequence" case (list of a list is itself; list of a tuple keeps order).
  // list() of other iterables (str/range/set/zip) is added via the iterator fold when needed.
  // (k-cell — list() constructs a NEW object)
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (list(VS:ValSeq),  .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (tuple(VS:ValSeq), .Vals)) => #alloc(list(VS)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), .Vals)                     => #alloc(list(.ValSeq)) ... </k>
  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("list")), (str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals))   => #alloc(list(charsOf(CS))) ... </k>
  syntax ValSeq ::= charsOf(IntSeq) [function, total]
  rule charsOf(.IntSeq)                => .ValSeq
  rule charsOf(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)) => vCons(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), charsOf(R))

  // ==== set(str) — distinct character codes =================================
  rule applyBuiltin("set", str(CS:IntSeq), .Vals) => setV(dedupCodes(CS))

  // ==== abs(int) ============================================================
  rule applyBuiltin("abs", I:Int, .Vals) => absInt(I)

  // ==== sum(iterable) — one #iterNext fold; intOf = int value of an int/bool ==
  syntax KItem ::= #sumAcc(Iterable, Int) | #sumCont(Int)
  rule <k> #sumAcc(IT:Iterable, ACC:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #sumCont(ACC) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int) => ACC ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #sumCont(ACC:Int)
        => #sumAcc(R, ACC +Int intOf(V)) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V) orBool isBool(V)

  syntax Int ::= intOf(Val) [function]
  rule intOf(I:Int)  => I
  rule intOf(B:Bool) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi

  // ==== all / any (short-circuiting #iterNext folds) ========================
  syntax KItem ::= #allAcc(Iterable) | "#allCont"
  rule <k> #allAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #allCont ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #allCont => true ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #allCont => #allAcc(R) ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #allCont => false ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  syntax KItem ::= #anyAcc(Iterable) | "#anyCont"
  rule <k> #anyAcc(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #anyCont ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #anyCont => false ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => true ... </k>
       requires truthy(V)
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #anyCont => #anyAcc(R) ... </k>
       requires notBool truthy(V)

  // ==== max / min over an iterable (#iterNext folds; first element seeds) ====
  syntax KItem ::= #maxAcc0(Iterable) | "#maxCont0" | #maxAcc(Iterable, Int) | #maxCont(Int)
  rule <k> #maxAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont0 ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont0 => #maxAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)
  rule <k> #maxAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #maxCont(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #maxCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #maxCont(M:Int)
        => #maxAcc(R, maxInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)

  syntax KItem ::= #minAcc0(Iterable) | "#minCont0" | #minAcc(Iterable, Int) | #minCont(Int)
  rule <k> #minAcc0(IT:Iterable) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont0 ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont0 => #minAcc(R, {V}:>Int) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)
  rule <k> #minAcc(IT:Iterable, M:Int) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #minCont(M) ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #minCont(M:Int) => M ... </k>
  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #minCont(M:Int)
        => #minAcc(R, minInt(M, {V}:>Int)) ... </k>
       requires isInt(V)

  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2

    89	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), (kwV("sep", str(S:IntSeq)), .Vals))
    90	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS), "split")), (str(S), .Vals)) ... </k>
    91	       [priority(39)]
    92	
    93	  // str.split(sep) — single-char separator, KEEPING empty parts (Python's sep-split; len == #sep + 1).
    94	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(str(CS:IntSeq), "split")), (str(iCons(SEP:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals))
    95	        => #alloc(list(splitSep(CS, SEP, .IntSeq))) ... </k>
    96	       [priority(40)]
    97	  syntax ValSeq ::= splitSep(IntSeq, Int, IntSeq) [function]  // remaining, sep code, current token
    98	  rule splitSep(.IntSeq, _SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq)              => vCons(str(CUR), .ValSeq)
    99	  rule splitSep(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq) => vCons(str(CUR), splitSep(R, SEP, .IntSeq))
   100	       requires C ==Int SEP
   101	  rule splitSep(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), SEP:Int, CUR:IntSeq) => splitSep(R, SEP, seqConcat(CUR, iCons(C, .IntSeq)))
   102	       requires notBool (C ==Int SEP)
   103	
   104	  rule applyMethod(str(CS:IntSeq), "replace", str(iCons(A:Int, .IntSeq)), str(iCons(B:Int, .IntSeq)), .Vals)
   105	    => str(replaceC(CS, A, B))
   106	  syntax IntSeq ::= replaceC(IntSeq, Int, Int) [function, total]
   107	  rule replaceC(.IntSeq, _:Int, _:Int)             => .IntSeq
   108	  rule replaceC(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int, B:Int) => iCons(B, replaceC(R, A, B)) requires C ==Int A
   109	  rule replaceC(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq), A:Int, B:Int) => iCons(C, replaceC(R, A, B)) requires notBool (C ==Int A)
   110	
   111	  // ==== char helpers =========================================================
   112	  syntax Bool ::= isUpperC(Int) [function, total]
   113	  rule isUpperC(C:Int) => C >=Int 65 andBool C <=Int 90
   114	
   115	  syntax Bool ::= isLowerC(Int) [function, total]
   116	  rule isLowerC(C:Int) => C >=Int 97 andBool C <=Int 122
   117	
   118	  syntax Bool ::= isAlphaC(Int) [function, total]
   119	  rule isAlphaC(C:Int) => isUpperC(C) orBool isLowerC(C)
   120	
   121	  syntax Bool ::= isDigitC(Int) [function, total]
   122	  rule isDigitC(C:Int) => C >=Int 48 andBool C <=Int 57
   123	
   124	  syntax Bool ::= hasUpper(IntSeq) [function, total]
   125	  rule hasUpper(.IntSeq) => false
   126	  rule hasUpper(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isUpperC(C) orBool hasUpper(S)
   127	
   128	  syntax Bool ::= hasLower(IntSeq) [function, total]
   129	  rule hasLower(.IntSeq) => false
   130	  rule hasLower(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isLowerC(C) orBool hasLower(S)
   131	
   132	  syntax Bool ::= allAlpha(IntSeq) [function, total]
   133	  rule allAlpha(.IntSeq) => true
   134	  rule allAlpha(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isAlphaC(C) andBool allAlpha(S)
   135	
   136	  syntax Bool ::= allDigit(IntSeq) [function, total]
   137	  rule allDigit(.IntSeq) => true
   138	  rule allDigit(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => isDigitC(C) andBool allDigit(S)
   139	
   140	  syntax Int ::= lowerC(Int) [function, total]
   141	
   142	  rule lowerC(C:Int) => C +Int 32 requires isUpperC(C)
   143	  rule lowerC(C:Int) => C         [owise]
   144	
   145	  syntax Int ::= upperC(Int) [function, total]
   146	  rule upperC(C:Int) => C -Int 32 requires isLowerC(C)
   147	  rule upperC(C:Int) => C         [owise]
   148	
   149	  syntax Int ::= swapC(Int) [function, total]
   150	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C +Int 32 requires isUpperC(C)
   151	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C -Int 32 requires isLowerC(C)
   152	  rule swapC(C:Int) => C         [owise]

   154	  syntax IntSeq ::= mapLower(IntSeq) [function, total]
   155	  rule mapLower(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
   156	  rule mapLower(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(lowerC(C), mapLower(S))

   158	  syntax IntSeq ::= mapUpper(IntSeq) [function, total]
   159	  rule mapUpper(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
   160	  rule mapUpper(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(upperC(C), mapUpper(S))

   163	  rule mapSwap(.IntSeq) => .IntSeq
   164	  rule mapSwap(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq)) => iCons(swapC(C), mapSwap(S))

     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))
    42	
    43	  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
    44	  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
    45	  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
    47	  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.
    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
    53	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B
    55	
    56	  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
    59	  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
    60	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
   109	  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   112	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   113	  rule buildVS(_:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .ValSeq
   114	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   115	
   116	  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   117	  rule buildIS(IS:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   118	    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   119	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   120	  rule buildIS(_:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .IntSeq
   121	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   122	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    48	        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    49	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    50	       [priority(40)]
    51	
    52	  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
    53	  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    54	    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
    55	       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
    56	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
    57	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
    58	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    59	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
    62	  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    64	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    65	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    66	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
    67	       [priority(40)]
    68	
    69	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    70	        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    71	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    72	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
    73	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    74	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    75	
    76	  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
    77	  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),

/audit-output/evidence/verification-body.content:
requires "reference-semantics/semantics.k"

module VERIFICATION-BODY-MUT
  imports MPY

  syntax KItem ::= "#checkIfLastCharMut" "(" Val ")"

  // Deliberate body mutation: compare the penultimate character to "x"
  // instead of the submitted body's " ".
  rule #checkIfLastCharMut(V:Val)
    => Call(
         closureVal(
           "txt",
           If(Compare(Call(Name("len"), Name("txt")),
                      CmpOp("==", Int(0))),
              Return(Bool(false)),
              .Stmts)
           If(UnaryOp("not",
                      Call(Attribute(
                             Subscript(Name("txt"), UnaryOp("-", Int(1))),
                             "isalpha"),
                           .Exprs)),
              Return(Bool(false)),
              .Stmts)
           If(Compare(Call(Name("len"), Name("txt")),
                      CmpOp("==", Int(1))),
              Return(Bool(true)),
              .Stmts)
           Return(Compare(
                    Subscript(Name("txt"), UnaryOp("-", Int(2))),
                    CmpOp("==", Str("x")))),
           0),
         V)

  rule isLen(seqConcat(P:IntSeq, iCons(A:Int, iCons(B:Int, .IntSeq))))
    => isLen(P) +Int 2
    [simplification]

  rule intSeqAt(
         seqConcat(P:IntSeq, iCons(A:Int, iCons(B:Int, .IntSeq))),
         isLen(P))
    => A
    [simplification]

  rule intSeqAt(
         seqConcat(P:IntSeq, iCons(A:Int, iCons(B:Int, .IntSeq))),
         isLen(P) +Int 1)
    => B
    [simplification]
endmodule

module BODY-SENSITIVITY-SPEC
  imports VERIFICATION-BODY-MUT

      #checkIfLastCharMut(

                      iCons(PREV:Int, iCons(LAST:Int, .IntSeq)))))

    </k>
    <env> 0 </env>
    <scopes>

    </scopes>
    <scopeLoc> 1 </scopeLoc>

    <stack> .List </stack>
    <ret> noRet </ret>
    <exc> NoExc </exc>
    <exit-code> 0 </exit-code>
    requires isLen(PREFIX) >=Int 0

         andBool PREV ==Int 32
endmodule

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /audit-output/REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial review
+
+Problem: `134-check-if-last-char-is-a-letter`  
+Condition: `semantics`  
+Rendered semantics mode: `SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`
+
+The candidate's six K claims reconstruct successfully and are non-vacuous, but
+they are not a legitimate proof of the real generated Python program over the
+HumanEval source-contract domain. The generated Python calls Unicode-aware
+`str.isalpha()`. The supplied semantics models that call with the ASCII-only
+predicate `isAlphaC`, and the trusted canonical implementation likewise admits
+only ASCII `a` through `z`. A concrete false-conclusion witness is `"é"`:
+
+- `/candidate/solution.py` returns `True`;
+- `/reference/canonical.py` returns `False`; and
+- the reconstructed K proof closes with `#Top` for code point `233` returning
+  `false`.
+
+Thus the proof establishes a theorem about the supplied ASCII code-sequence
+model, not partial correctness of the real submitted Python program. This is a
+material language/domain gap and maps to `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT` under the benchmark
+decision boundary.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+`/audit-input.json` declares `record_layout =
+legacy-selected-stage1`, `semantics_mode = SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`, and maps all
+launcher mounts through `container_paths`. I treated the host provenance paths
+as metadata and inspected only the mounted container paths.
+
+Integrity findings:
+
+- `/audit-campaign-lock.json` is a regular readable file. Its parsed object is
+  structurally identical to `audit_input["audit_campaign"]`, and its SHA-256 is
+  the recorded
+  `ad5dfcc006af70c4d0d2c6641f0878a6c54a266e9ad2b54cd225b2381a78d745`.
+- All records required for `legacy-selected-stage1` are present, readable, and
+  nonsymlinked: `/run.json`, `/task.json`, `/generation-result.json`,
+  `invocation.json`, `metrics.json`, `codex-last.txt`, `codex-output.log`,
+  `prompt.txt`, the structured JSONL trace, and the present `usage.json`.
+  Historical `runtime-metrics.json` is not required for this legacy layout.
+- Recorded file hashes for the campaign lock, run/task/result manifests,
+  invocation, metrics, usage, prompt, Codex output/last message, trace file,
+  canonical, trusted prompt, and translator all match independent SHA-256
+  calculations.
+- All 181 structured-trace lines parse as JSON. The 10,318-line Codex log and
+  all other required generation records were read and summarized. Their
+  `KPROVE_PASSED` marker is only an untrusted generation claim.
+- `/candidate/prompt.py` is byte-identical to `/reference/prompt.py`, and
+  `/candidate/py2mpy.py` is byte-identical to `/reference/py2mpy.py`.
+- The required trusted `/reference/reference-semantics` mount is present.
+  `diff -qr --no-dereference` finds no missing, additional, changed, or
+  mistyped entry in `/candidate/reference-semantics`. No symlink exists
+  anywhere in the candidate, reference, or generation-evidence trees.
+- Every candidate file was independently hashed. No launcher-owned mount or
+  required provenance record is absent or unreadable, so there is no audit
+  infrastructure breach.
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `evidence/stage1_integrity.sh`
+- `evidence/stage1_integrity.log` — command exit 0,
+  `STAGE1_INTEGRITY_OK`
+- `evidence/generation_record_summary.py`
+- `evidence/generation_record_summary.log` — command exit 0
+
+Stage 1 result: **PASS**.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and candidate-versus-canonical checks
+
+### Source contract
+
+The trusted prompt requires a function on a Python string that returns true
+exactly when the final character is alphabetic and is not part of a
+space-delimited word. The trusted canonical makes the intended predicate
+precise:
+
+1. split on the literal space;
+2. take the last piece;
+3. require that piece to have length one; and
+4. require its lowercased character code to be in ASCII `97..122`.
+
+Equivalently, the canonical returns true precisely when the string is one ASCII
+letter, or when it ends in an ASCII letter whose immediately preceding
+character is a space. Empty strings, trailing spaces, nonletters, and
+non-ASCII letters return false.
+
+### Translation identity
+
+The trusted command
+
+```text
+python3 /reference/py2mpy.py /tmp/audit-work/candidate/solution.py
+```
+
+created `solution.regenerated.mpy`. It is byte-identical to the submitted
+`solution.mpy`; both have SHA-256
+`9e03fdeff3da93d08bca16e915284912d738d1557badd000f682a8c690d61395`.
+The translator and comparison both exited 0. See
+`evidence/translator_regeneration.log`.
+
+### Independent differential test
+
+`evidence/differential_test.py` independently imports the trusted canonical and
+the generated candidate. It exercises:
+
+- all four documented examples;
+- empty, one-character, two-character, spacing, letter, digit, and punctuation
+  branch boundaries;
+- every string through length four over the branch-focused alphabet
+  `' aA0!?éβ'`; and
+- 1,000 fixed-seed generated strings up to length 24.
+
+Exact command: `python3 /audit-output/evidence/differential_test.py`.
+It tested 5,577 unique inputs, found 163 mismatches, and exited 1 as designed
+when mismatches exist. Representative counterexamples are:
+
+```text
+input='é'  canonical=False  candidate=True
+input='β'  canonical=False  candidate=True
+input=' é' canonical=False  candidate=True
+input='a β' canonical=False candidate=True
+```
+
+All documented and ASCII branch cases agree; the divergence is specifically
+the generated use of Unicode-aware `str.isalpha()` versus the canonical ASCII
+test. Complete bounded output is in `evidence/differential_test.log`.
+
+This is a material divergence on the unrestricted Python `str` domain. The
+prompt contains no ASCII-only precondition.
+
+Stage 2 result: **FAIL (material program/canonical divergence)**.
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+I copied candidate source artifacts to `/tmp/audit-work/candidate` and created
+new output definitions named `audit-runtime-kompiled` and
+`audit-verification-kompiled`. No candidate-built definition or cache was
+reused. The available toolchain is K `v7.1.293`; see
+`evidence/tool_versions.log`.
+
+Fresh build and execution commands:
+
+```text
+kompile reference-semantics/semantics.k --backend llvm \
+  --main-module MPY-KRUN --syntax-module MPY-SYNTAX \
+  --output-definition audit-runtime-kompiled
+
+krun concrete_tests.mpy --definition audit-runtime-kompiled --output pretty
+
+kompile verification.k --backend haskell \
+  --main-module VERIFICATION --syntax-module VERIFICATION \
+  --output-definition audit-verification-kompiled
+```
+
+All three exited 0. The concrete run ended with `.K`, `NoExc`, and exit code
+zero. Logs are `evidence/llvm_kompile.log`,
+`evidence/concrete_krun.log`, and `evidence/haskell_kompile.log`.
+
+To avoid trusting a single aggregate proof run, I copied each submitted claim
+unchanged into a separate module in `evidence/positive-claims.k` and ran:
+
+```text
+kprove positive-claims.k --definition audit-verification-kompiled \
+  --spec-module <MODULE>
+```
+
+| Claim module | Result | Evidence |
+|---|---:|---|
+| `SPEC-EMPTY` | exit 0, `#Top` | `evidence/kprove_spec_empty.log` |
+| `SPEC-ONE-ALPHA` | exit 0, `#Top` | `evidence/kprove_spec_one_alpha.log` |
+| `SPEC-ONE-NONALPHA` | exit 0, `#Top` | `evidence/kprove_spec_one_nonalpha.log` |
+| `SPEC-LONG-TRUE` | exit 0, `#Top` | `evidence/kprove_spec_long_true.log` |
+| `SPEC-LONG-LAST-NONALPHA` | exit 0, `#Top` | `evidence/kprove_spec_long_last_nonalpha.log` |
+| `SPEC-LONG-PREV-NOT-SPACE` | exit 0, `#Top` | `evidence/kprove_spec_long_prev_not_space.log` |
+
+The positive target-proof gate therefore reconstructs successfully. This says
+only that the claims close under the supplied theory and proof-local rules; it
+does not repair the real-program mismatch found in Stage 2.
+
+Stage 3 result: **PASS (formal closure reconstructed)**.
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Plain-language claims
+
+The six formal claims partition constructor-form `IntSeq` strings as follows:
+
+1. empty returns `false`;
+2. length one with `isAlphaC(C)` returns `true`;
+3. length one with `notBool isAlphaC(C)` returns `false`;
+4. length at least two, ASCII-alpha last code, and penultimate code `32`
+   returns `true`;
+5. length at least two with non-ASCII-alpha/nonalpha last code returns `false`;
+6. length at least two with ASCII-alpha last code and penultimate code not
+   `32` returns `false`.
+
+For long strings,
+`seqConcat(PREFIX, iCons(PREV, iCons(LAST, .IntSeq)))` represents an arbitrary
+prefix followed by its last two codes. `isLen(PREFIX) >=Int 0` holds for every
+finite constructor sequence, so it does not bound the source length. The
+alpha/nonalpha and space/nonspace cases are disjoint and exhaustive under the
+supplied `isAlphaC`.
+
+Each RHS is a concrete boolean. No result variable is free, no implication
+weakens equivalence, and the complete initial/final cells constrain normal
+return with an empty heap and stack, restored environment, `NoExc`, and exit
+code zero.
+
+### Satisfiability
+
+`evidence/witness_comparison.py` exhibits one ground witness for every entry
+precondition:
+
+| Claim | Witness | Claimed/canonical/candidate |
+|---|---|---|
+| empty | `""` | `False` |
+| one alpha | `"a"` | `True` |
+| one nonalpha | `"7"` | `False` |
+| long true | `" a"` | `True` |
+| long last nonalpha | `" !"` | `False` |
+| long previous not space | `"aa"` | `False` |
+
+The script exited 0; see `evidence/witness_comparison.log`.
+
+### Constructor-level program identity
+
+The entry rule does not return a summary oracle. It constructs a
+`closureVal` and sends it through the fixed call, frame, branch, subscript,
+method, and return rules.

real Python `str.isalpha()` on the intended unrestricted string domain.

```text
input value: str(iCons(233, .IntSeq))  // Python "é"
```

exception-only difference: the one-character nonalpha claim directly proves

## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test

The candidate supplied no `spec-vacuity.k`; no candidate mutation evidence was
trusted.

I created `evidence/spec-vacuity-fresh.k`, changing the empty-string result
obligation from `false` to `true`. Its precondition is concretely satisfied by
`""`, for which both Python implementations return `False`.

```text
# exit 0

  --spec-module SPEC-VACUITY-FRESH

```

The first command establishes that the mutation parses/builds. The second
fails for the expected unmet result, not a parser error, missing import,
timeout, or unrelated crash. See `evidence/fresh_mutation_dry_run.log` and
`evidence/fresh_mutation_kprove.log`.

Stage 6 result: **PASS (proof is result-constraining and non-vacuous)**.

## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting

### What the successful reachability proof establishes

Conditional on the supplied K definition and the four proof-local rules, the
six claims establish partial correctness of the directly constructed closure
over finite constructor code sequences:

- empty returns false;
- a one-code string returns the ASCII `isAlphaC` classification; and
- a longer string returns true exactly when its final code is an ASCII letter
  and its penultimate code is `32`.

The proof executes the submitted constructor body and constrains a concrete
boolean result. It is universal in prefix length; it is not finite unrolling or
example-only proof.

### Trust and assumption ledger

| Boundary | Influence | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Trusted `py2mpy.py` transliteration | Program-term identity | Acceptable launcher trust boundary; byte regeneration was independently checked. It does not validate Python/K semantic equivalence. |
| Supplied K core, cells, call/frame, branches, returns, integer/string indexing, and builtins | Control, state, returned value | Required named fixed-semantics boundary. The used slice is operationally complete for the submitted constructors. |
| Supplied `isalpha`/`isAlphaC` equations | Branch and final result | **Illegitimate for the real submitted Python program on Unicode inputs.** The U+00E9 witness demonstrates the wrong result. |
| Direct-closure entry adapter | Binding, body, lexical environment | Mechanically pins name/parameter/body and scope; safe for this nonrecursive return property. It omits the persistent module function binding, so it is not a theorem about complete module poststate. |
| Three proof-local suffix simplifications | Symbolic length and final-two indexing | Mathematically valid by induction on finite constructor sequences; no false witness or conflicting overlap found. Universal bridge-free `kprove` evidence is absent, so this remains an informal-induction limitation. |
| 25 supplied opaque/external symbols | Potential values in unrelated language features | Unreachable from this program and all six claims; no dependency on a float, sort, or MD5 oracle. |
| K builtin mathematics and SMT reasoning | Integer inequalities and boolean partitions | Ordinary low-level proof trust boundary. |
| Termination | Whether a result is reached | The theorem is partial correctness. Concrete runs terminate, but differential/concrete tests are finite evidence, not a termination theorem. |
| Differential and witness tests | Python/canonical adequacy bridge | Reproducible finite evidence only. Here they expose a counterexample; they are not used as a substitute for K proof. |

### Gate and verdict accounting

- Fresh formal reconstruction: pass.
- Result constraint/non-vacuity: pass.
- Proof-local body execution and constructor pinning: pass for the return
  property, with a module-binding observation.
- Proof-local simplification validation: mathematically supported, but lacks
  bridge-free universal machine closure; evidence limitation only.
- Real-program/source-contract adequacy: fail. The generated Python diverges
  from the canonical, and the K model proves a result that is false of that
  Python program on `"é"`.

The formal artifact is therefore at best sound-but-limited to an ASCII
interpretation. The benchmark explicitly maps material narrowing or
mis-modeling of the HumanEval source-contract domain to `FAIL / NOT_LEGIT`,
not to `CONCERNS / LEGIT`.

VERDICT: FAIL
LEGITIMACY: NOT_LEGIT
